tasks.short: Distribute site brochures, show presentations and explain operations

steps.what: Find and check current brochures and audiovisual material for the tour site
Distribute the appropriate brochures to tour participants
Set up and show the checked audiovisual presentation to the group
Explain establishment processes and operations and answer tour participants' questions

tasks.design: Use direct current-material references in {DOCS}. Keep brochure distribution, operation of {OTHER}, the audiovisual presentation equipment, and personal explanations separate and fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current language and presentation version repeats preparation navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native current-material links can remove that search.
tasks.still_hard: Participants need responsive explanation and help understanding the site.
tasks.human_edge: Connect the presentation with what the group can actually see and ask.
tasks.altitude: Reduce site-material navigation without replacing guide interaction.

reach.learn: Use the appropriate current language and material version

evidence.claim: Current material links can reduce repeated version searching; physical distribution and live explanation remain human.

assumptions: The brochures and presentation are existing site assets. No new script, inventory record, visitor log or presentation completion report is added.

The guide verifies site, material version and group language in s1; checking time remains inside eight retained preparation hours. Missing or incompatible files require manual selection and equipment setup.

Direct version and language references remove 2 of 10 material-search hours. Presentation setup, physical distribution and explanation remain fully retained; existing playback runtime is not eligible human labour.
No automatic presentation start or material send is proposed. Each actual public delivery has its own content/recipient gate.
research_questions: Does a current-material link remove actual search without increasing version checking?

already_counted.description: Find and verify actual site material

approvals.approved_version: Exact brochure version and intended group checked before distribution; changed content or group requires rechecking
Exact audiovisual file and present audience checked before showing; changed file or audience requires rechecking
Exact process explanation and answers delivered to the current group; changed questions or content require guide reconsideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=98, gross 2 less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5 net. Already current material links retaining 9.5 preparation hours have the half-hour saving offset by upkeep. Partly useful language/version indexing retaining 8.5 preparation plus other 90 and 0.5 upkeep yields 1 net. Brochure handling, presentation operation and personal explanations remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train guides and volunteers in site guiding

steps.what: Review current tour content, safety guidance and trainee learning needs
Write session guidance and exercises using the existing guide training format
Send final session guidance to the participating guides and site volunteers
Train guides and volunteers through explanation, demonstrations and practice
Observe trainee guiding practice and discuss improvement needs
outputs: observed learning and further support needs

steps.what: Enter actual training completion and support needs in the existing training register
inputs: observed learning and further support needs

tasks.design: Reuse current tour references and the existing session format in {DOCS}. Keep guidance writing and sending before live training, with observed completion entered afterwards in the existing register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated tour references and session structure add training preparation work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and established training forms preserve unchanged context.
tasks.still_hard: Guiding performance and judgement require observed practice.
tasks.human_edge: Coach explanation, group awareness and safe responses in context.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated training-material handling while retaining practice and coaching.

reach.learn: Distinguish training attendance from observed guiding ability

evidence.claim: Existing tour references and training formats can reduce repeated preparation; guide training savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: The session guidance and training register are existing records used to prepare training and follow up guide readiness. No transcript or new coaching log is created.

The guide verifies current tour and safety versions in s1, produces actual session guidance in s2, observes practice in s5 and captures trainee, session, completion and further needs in s6. All capture is counted; missing completion evidence is checked manually.

Current references remove 2 of 10 preparation hours. Reusing unchanged tour explanations and exercise headings removes 3 of 15 writing hours; stable register context removes 0.5 of 5 completion-entry hours.
Volunteers are members of the site's operational team for this internal handoff. Ordinary author saves have no self-approval; the actual guidance send has its own gate.
unknowns: Existing training format and completion-register use
research_questions: Does existing content reuse remove actual preparation after checking current safety guidance?

already_counted.description: Write actual session content and later completion evidence

incremental.description: Maintain current references and existing form headings

approvals.approved_version: Exact final session guidance and participating team recipient set checked in s2; changed content or recipients invalidate the check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=94.5, gross 5.5 less 0.5 upkeep gives 5 net. New sites requiring wholly different guidance retain all preparation and session writing, leaving only half an hour of register structure removed and offset by upkeep. Comparable tours retaining nine preparation, 13 session-writing and 4.5 completion hours plus other 70 and 0.5 upkeep yield 3 net. Actual send, live training and observed practice remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain wildlife, habitats and relevant activity regulations

steps.what: Clarify the visitor's wildlife question, location and intended activity
Identify likely wildlife from observed features and check the proposed identification

loop.purpose: Suggest a wildlife identification from the guide's observation or photograph
loop.input: Actual observed features or photograph with location and date
loop.output: Candidate species with visible distinguishing features and uncertainty
loop.check: Guide compares proposed features and habitat against the observation and a species reference, rejecting unsupported identification
loop.stop: One alternative; poor image, uncertain features or disagreement produces an explicitly uncertain answer or manual reference lookup
loop.why_not_simpler: Visual species variation cannot be handled by a short fixed lookup table

steps.what: Determine which species and habitat information applies to the visitor's question
Find and verify applicable current hunting, fishing or site regulations
Provide wildlife, habitat and verified regulation information with its limitations

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, a species-identification application and official activity-rule viewer, with references in {DOCS}. A bounded identification proposal assists the guide, while current rule lookup and the final visitor explanation remain checked human work; no permit determination is generated from species guesses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Species-reference searching and official-rule navigation interrupt on-site answers.
tasks.enabler_now: Photo identification and direct official map references support these distinct operations.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain wildlife and location-specific restrictions need careful qualification.
tasks.human_edge: Know when the evidence does not support a confident identification or permission answer.
tasks.altitude: Find relevant wildlife and rule context faster without automating visitor advice.

reach.learn: Separate species information from official activity permission

evidence.claim: ObsIdentify identifies European wild species from photographs.
VISplanner supplies location-specific fishing permission information; it does not establish hunting permission or species safety.

assumptions: The output is an on-site explanation, not a new species log, visitor record or written legal opinion. No unnecessary record-writing step is added.

The guide obtains location, date, intended activity and relevant permit type in s1, captures the observation or photograph in s2 and verifies current official reference information in s4. Capture and checks are included in 17.5 identification and 15 rule-lookup hours; missing permit or location context requires manual clarification and no permission claim.

Identification assistance removes 7.5 of 25 species-search hours after photo capture, feature checking and fallback. Direct official map references remove 5 of 20 rule-navigation hours; actual applicability checking remains.
No machine sends advice or grants permission. The guide delivers the actual explanation and its uncertainty; official rule changes require reference maintenance.
unknowns: Identification accuracy for local species and images
Availability and freshness of official local rules
research_questions: Does photo assistance reduce lookup time after rejecting uncertain identifications and checking official location rules?

already_counted.description: Capture observation and check species proposal and rule applicability

incremental.description: Maintain official references and review identification failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact clarifying questions and activity discussion with the present visitor; changed circumstances require reconsideration
Exact species explanation, uncertainty and current applicable rule information delivered to the visitor; changed location, permit or content requires renewed checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=87.5, gross 12.5 less 2 upkeep gives 10.5 net. Poor images and unfamiliar permit conditions retain all identification and 18 rule hours, offsetting the two hours removed with upkeep. Recognizable species retaining 20 identification and 17 rule hours plus other 55 and 2 upkeep yield 6 net. Wildlife relevance judgement and visitor communication remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach safe activity skills and equipment use

steps.what: Check participants, physical equipment and the current activity conditions
Choose the appropriate teaching method and participant-specific equipment advice
Teach activity skills and demonstrate proper climbing methods or equipment use
Observe participant practice and correct unsafe technique or equipment handling

tasks.design: Retain participant and equipment checks, technique choice, demonstration and observed practice. An instruction template in {DOCS} does not remove these hands-on teaching operations; no newly required skill log is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on physical technique and immediate safety judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No identified software operation replaces this direct teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Unsafe practice requires immediate correction matched to the participant.
tasks.human_edge: See what the participant is actually doing and adjust the instruction.

reach.learn: Recognize when a demonstration has not produced safe practice

evidence.claim: Physical skill demonstrations and observed safety correction remain human without an identified repeated record operation to remove.

assumptions: The task is teaching technique and advising on actual equipment. It does not specify writing a training certificate, equipment inspection register or participant progress log.
The guide produces condition observations in s1 and actual practice observations in s4, with all capture time retained. No machine consumes an assumed competence or equipment-safe flag.

A native document view or template removes none of the identified physical checks, participant judgement or direct instruction. No routine lookup is identified in this immediate skill-teaching boundary.
No new system or recurring upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Whether any local activity requires a separate existing written competence or inspection record
research_questions: Does current observation reveal an actual lookup or record operation within this teaching task?

already_counted.description: Check teaching conditions and observe actual participant practice

incremental.description: No new tool or capture workflow

approvals.approved_version: Exact demonstration and equipment advice for the checked participants and conditions; changed content or conditions require renewed judgement
Exact corrective instruction for the current observed practice; new hazards or participant needs require immediate reconsideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=100 and no upkeep gives zero. Familiar equipment and unfamiliar participant ability both retain condition checks, technique judgement, demonstration and correction; no actual duplicated data operation is identified for removal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain live guiding and safety instruction while reducing genuine material, training and reference repetition.
reach: Give visitors qualified wildlife and rule information
Support other guides through observed practice
skills_to_grow: Verify identification proposals against actual features
Separate training materials, sends and later completion entry
role.ambitious_version: A guide with current supporting material and less repeated preparation who personally explains sites, supports visitors and teaches safe activity skills.
